brief.headline: Memory supercycle intact but sentiment cracks: Samsung/Hynix down 10%+ on valuation reset and 2027 price-peak fears despite HBM4 ramp and $725B hyperscaler capex
brief.summary: <cite index="39-1,39-10,39-11">SK Hynix and Samsung stock plunged more than 10% in Seoul on July 28 as investors reassessed AI boom risks</cite>, with <cite index="39-12">KOSPI dropping 7.41% and triggering program trading restrictions</cite>. <cite index="41-4,41-5">Broker reports flagging memory price peak in 2027 drove today's weakness, though Standard Chartered notes risk-reward has improved at current valuations</cite>. <cite index="1-7,1-8">Samsung shipped industry-first commercial HBM4 with 11.7Gbps transfer speed and 4nm logic base die, marking first-in-industry achievement</cite>, while <cite index="18-2,18-6">five largest US hyperscalers committed $660-690 billion in 2026 capex, nearly doubling 2025 levels</cite>. <cite index="12-2">TrendForce projects conventional DRAM contract prices to rise 13-18% QoQ in Q3 2026, marking a slowdown from roughly 60% Q2 jumps</cite>.
brief.pair_trade_view: Short-term: neutral to slight Hynix overweight. <cite index="39-3,39-4,39-5">The selloff is a sentiment/valuation reset, not proof HBM demand collapsed; Hynix is the cleanest HBM beneficiary tied to Nvidia-class accelerators</cite>, while <cite index="39-8,39-9">Samsung has more exposure to conventional memory and foundry cycles where China capacity push can pressure prices, making it easier for investors to rotate away</cite>. <cite index="1-7,1-8">Samsung's HBM4 mass production and commercial shipment milestone</cite> versus <cite index="4-1">SK Hynix noting HBM3E will account for about two-thirds of total HBM shipments in 2026</cite> suggests Samsung is accelerating next-gen share gains, but Hynix maintains <cite index="5-11,5-12">62% HBM shipment share in Q2 2025 and 57% revenue share in Q3, with Goldman Sachs expecting Hynix to sustain over 50% total HBM market share through at least 2026</cite>. Medium-term tactical lean Hynix on purer HBM leverage; long-term both benefit from structural HBM shift.

memory_cycle.stage: Late expansion / early maturity with bifurcated dynamics
memory_cycle.notes: <cite index="10-2,10-9">TrendForce projects global memory market at $551.6 billion in 2026 with DRAM revenue up 144% YoY hitting $404.3 billion</cite>. <cite index="8-7,8-8">Samsung, SK Hynix, and Micron permanently redirected wafer production toward HBM for AI data centers, removing supply from consumer market while cloud providers place open-ended purchase commitments, creating structural shortage</cite>. <cite index="12-2,12-3,12-4">Q3 2026 DRAM contract price increases projected at 13-18% QoQ, substantial but a marked slowdown from 60% Q2 jumps, driven by consumer electronics manufacturers' unwillingness to absorb higher costs rather than improved supply—memory remains in short supply but consumers no longer willing to pay ever-higher prices</cite>. <cite index="10-1">DDR4 spot prices ($2.10/Gbit) now exceed HBM3E contract prices ($1.70/Gbit)</cite>. Hyperscaler-driven HBM/server DRAM demand remains structural; consumer DRAM/NAND pricing hitting demand destruction. Cycle duration extends to 2027-2028 peak per broker consensus.

brief.hbm_pulse: <cite index="1-7,1-8">Samsung began mass production of industry-leading HBM4 with 11.7Gbps consistent transfer speed capable of up to 13Gbps, shipping commercial products to customers—a first in the industry</cite>. <cite index="1-1,1-4">HBM4 bandwidth increased 2.7x versus HBM3E to max 3.3 TB/s, with 40% power efficiency improvement via low-voltage TSV and PDN optimization, plus 10% better thermal resistance and 30% heat dissipation gains</cite>. <cite index="4-1">SK Hynix noted HBM3E will remain dominant product in 2026, accounting for about two-thirds of total HBM shipments, while HBM4 gradually gains traction</cite>. <cite index="2-2,2-4">HBM3E supply remains tight and lags demand as Samsung and SK Hynix prioritize ramping next-gen HBM4; ongoing launches of AI accelerators using HBM3E by global big tech keep demand on steady growth path</cite>. <cite index="2-5">HBM3E demand exceeded expectations following approval for Nvidia H200 AI chip exports to China, with each H200 incorporating six stacks of HBM3E</cite>. Pricing: <cite index="2-8,2-9">AI-driven demand reshaping memory market, with HBM3E pricing expected to trend higher amid tightening supply; sources report Samsung and SK Hynix plan ~20% HBM3E price hike for 2026</cite>.

news_pulse.headline: Samsung ships industry-first commercial HBM4 with 11.7Gbps speed, 4nm logic die
news_pulse.implication: Samsung secures early leadership in HBM4 market ahead of peers; mass production with 2.7x bandwidth improvement vs HBM3E and 40% power efficiency gain strengthens competitive position in next-gen AI accelerator supply chain. Material positive for foundry/logic revenue mix and HBM ASP trajectory.

news_pulse.headline: SK Hynix, Samsung plunge 10%+ as KOSPI drops 7.4%, program trading halted
news_pulse.implication: Valuation reset and sentiment shift on AI financing concerns plus broker notes citing 2027 memory price peak. Technical damage severe but fundamentals intact—hyperscaler capex remains structural, HBM supply still lags demand. Near-term volatility likely persists into Q2 earnings (July 29 for Hynix).

news_pulse.headline: Hyperscalers commit $660-690B in 2026 capex, nearly doubling 2025 levels
news_pulse.implication: Amazon $200B, Alphabet $175-185B, Meta $115-135B, Microsoft $120B+, Oracle $50B. All report supply-constrained rather than demand-constrained. Direct positive for HBM/server DRAM/SSD demand—confirms structural tailwind despite equity market repricing.

news_pulse.headline: DRAM prices hit all-time highs; Q2 contract prices up 58-63% QoQ but Q3 slows to 13-18%
news_pulse.implication: Consumer demand destruction evident—pricing power moderating as OEMs refuse to absorb further increases. Server/HBM pricing dynamics remain decoupled. Revenue growth shifts from volume to mix (HBM/server) as commodity DRAM QoQ gains compress. Gross margin trajectory still positive but momentum peaking.

news_pulse.headline: DDR4 spot prices ($2.10/Gbit) now exceed HBM3E contract prices ($1.70/Gbit)
news_pulse.implication: Inverted pricing structure highlights extreme consumer DRAM shortage vs. locked-in hyperscaler HBM contracts. Spot buyers paying premium to contract—procurement risk elevated for non-contracted customers. Reinforces bifurcated market: consumer pain, hyperscaler contracts insulated.

news_pulse.headline: TSMC CoWoS supply-demand gap narrowing from 20% to 10% by end-2026
news_pulse.implication: TSMC CoWoS capacity reaching 115,000-140,000 wpm by end-2026, up from 13,000 wpm end-2023. Easing packaging bottleneck should accelerate Nvidia Blackwell/Rubin ramps and HBM attach rates in 2H26-2027. Positive for HBM volume growth but also signals hyperscaler GPU supply improving—watch for pricing pressure on memory content per accelerator.

news_pulse.headline: Samsung, SK Hynix reportedly plan ~20% HBM3E price hike for 2026 as Nvidia H200, ASIC demand rises
news_pulse.implication: HBM3E supply tight as suppliers prioritize HBM4 ramp; H200 export approval to China drove unexpected demand spike (6 stacks HBM3E per H200). 2026 HBM revenue mix forecast ~55% HBM4 / 45% HBM3E. Pricing power intact through at least 1H26; watch for mix shift impact on blended ASPs as HBM4 share rises.

news_pulse.headline: SK Hynix Q2 2026 earnings July 29: analysts forecast ~₩84T revenue, record operating margin
news_pulse.implication: Earnings catalyst tomorrow could stabilize sentiment if DRAM/NAND pricing commentary confirms sustained tightness and HBM4 ramp visibility. Risk: any demand-side caution or 2H26 visibility comments could exacerbate selloff given today's repricing. Watch HBM3E vs HBM4 mix guidance and hyperscaler order visibility.

brief.derivatives_signal: Implied volatility likely elevated post-selloff; KOSPI program trading restrictions triggered at -7.4% suggest circuit-breaker risk if selling accelerates. No specific options flow data available from payload, but ADR/local equity dislocation (Hynix US ADRs closed Monday at $143.02 below $149 offer price per search results) indicates hedging pressure and potential basis trades. Near-dated puts likely rich; consider selling elevated IV if bullish on earnings stabilization. Watch for gamma unwind if names attempt to reclaim intraday lows.
watch_for_next_3h: SK Hynix Q2 2026 earnings (July 29, pre-market KST)—revenue, operating margin, HBM3E/HBM4 mix, and hyperscaler order visibility commentary will set near-term sentiment; any caution on 2H26 demand could extend selloff
KOSPI circuit-breaker risk if semis extend losses—program trading restrictions already triggered at -7.41%; further declines could prompt institutional deleveraging and contagion to ADRs/ETFs
Micron, NVDA pre-market reaction to Seoul rout—semiconductor basket already down $1.5T since June 25 per Yahoo Finance; watch for US memory/AI names to stabilize or extend weakness
Broker downgrades or target cuts citing 2027 price-peak thesis—Standard Chartered noted 2027 memory price peak view driving today's weakness; any sell-side capitulation could mark near-term bottom
Samsung earnings release timing confirmation (expected this week per search results)—comparison to Hynix results will clarify relative HBM4 vs HBM3E positioning and foundry exposure impact
